knowledge_point.title: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix

question.:question/problem:
$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 6 & -4 \\ 12 & 1 & -10 \\ -2 & -6 & -7\end{bmatrix},\,B=\begin{bmatrix}-70 & 0 & 56 \\ 12 & 1 & -10 \\ 70 & 0 & -67\end{bmatrix}
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form $R_{i}:=R_{i}+kR_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above and below $a_{22}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}2 & 6 & -4 \\ 12 & 1 & -10 \\ -2 & -6 & -7\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{1}:=R_{1}-6R_{2}}\begin{bmatrix}-70 & 0 & 56 \\ 12 & 1 & -10 \\ -2 & -6 & -7\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{3}:=R_{3}+6R_{2}}\begin{bmatrix}-70 & 0 & 56 \\ 12 & 1 & -10 \\ 70 & 0 & -67\end{bmatrix}=B
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$R_{1}:=R_{1}-6R_{2}$ and $R_{3}:=R_{3}+6R_{2}$.
